name: Acute primary angle closure
summary: Sudden blockage of aqueous outflow: very high IOP, oedematous cornea, shallow chamber, fixed mid-dilated pupil and ciliary flush.

revealed_by.diffuse: Steamy hazy cornea with a dull, broken reflex; the iris and pupil are still seen through it. Ciliary flush densest around the limbus; fixed, vertically oval mid-dilated pupil.
revealed_by.optic_section_cornea: Thick hazy corneal section; very shallow central chamber, so the corneal and lens beams almost touch.

teaching_points: Do not dilate; check IOP and the fellow eye's angle.
The cornea is hazy, not the lens; do not mistake it for a white cataract.
Treat urgently to lower IOP, then laser peripheral iridotomy to both eyes.

provenance.source: Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology, 9th ed.; EGS Terminology and Guidelines for Glaucoma, 5th ed.
